title: Lakshya Sen Seeks Redemption at China Masters as Lanier Withdraws
excerpt: India's top shuttler will now face Canada's Victor Lai in the opening round after newly crowned world champion Alex Lanier pulled out of the BWF Super 750 event in Shenzhen.
body:
• Lakshya Sen will open his China Masters 2026 campaign against Canada's Victor Lai after world champion Alex Lanier withdrew from the BWF Super 750 tournament in Shenzhen
  • Sen is looking to bounce back after a shock second-round exit at the BWF World Championships, where he fell to world No. 92 Garret Tan
  • Eleven of India's 20-player Asian Games squad are competing in Shenzhen, making the China Masters a key rehearsal for the continental showpiece in Aichi-Nagoya
  • PV Sindhu and Ayush Shetty have both withdrawn from the tournament, leaving Sen and Kidambi Srikanth to lead India's singles challenge

Lakshya Sen will lead India's challenge at the China Masters 2026 in Shenzhen, seeking to put a disappointing BWF World Championships campaign behind him as a strong Indian contingent begins its preparation for the Asian Games later this month.

The BWF Super 750 tournament at the Shenzhen Sports Centre Gymnasium runs from September 1 to 6, with a prize purse of $1.25 million.

Lanier Withdraws, Lai Steps In

Sen was originally drawn against newly crowned world champion Alex Lanier of France in a blockbuster first-round clash. Lanier made history at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi by becoming the first Frenchman to win the men's singles world title. However, Lanier has withdrawn from the China Masters following his title-winning run, and Sen will now face Canada's Victor Lai in the opening round.

The change does not necessarily make Sen's path easier. Lai reached the World Championships semifinals in New Delhi, defeating former world champion Loh Kean Yew along the way before losing to Lanier. The Canadian leads his head-to-head against Sen 2-1 in 2026, having won their Thomas Cup and China Open encounters after Sen took their first meeting in the All England Open semifinals.

Bouncing Back From the Worlds

Sen, ranked world No. 13, endured an early exit at the World Championships. After beating Austria's Collins Valentine Filimon in the first round, he fell to USA's Garret Tan — ranked 92nd in the world — in a closely fought second-round match that ended 19-21, 21-19, 21-17 in Tan's favor.

The result was a setback for a player who became the first Indian male shuttler to reach an Olympic semifinal at Paris 2024 and finished runner-up at the All England Championships earlier this season. The China Masters offers Sen an immediate opportunity to reset before the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, which begin on September 19.

India's Squad in Shenzhen

Former world No. 1 Kidambi Srikanth, who reached the US Open final in June, joins Sen in men's singles. In doubles, fourth-seeded pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty — ranked world No. 5 — spearhead India's campaign. The pair ended a two-year wait for an international title by winning the Singapore Badminton Open in May and reached the World Championships quarterfinals.

India's women's singles contingent features three rising players. Unnati Hooda, 18, made her World Championships debut and is ranked world No. 25. Tanvi Sharma, 17, won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Taipei Open this season. Devika Sihag claimed the Thailand Masters title earlier this year.

Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu and Ayush Shetty — who stunned 2025 world champion Shi Yuqi in the opening round at the Worlds — have both withdrawn from the tournament. Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, who won a historic bronze at the World Championships, are also absent.

Asian Games Dress Rehearsal

As many as 11 of India's 20-player Asian Games badminton squad will be in action in Shenzhen, including Sen, Srikanth, Rankireddy, Shetty, and all three women's singles players. The China Masters is the only major BWF World Tour event between the World Championships and the Asian Games, which run from September 19 to October 4 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

No Indian player has won the China Masters since the tournament's inception in 2005. With their Asian Games preparations on the line and a point to prove after a mixed World Championships, India's contingent will be keen to change that record this week.
